children: A working paper written on 2026-11-16, published nearly as written. Local file paths, private repository names and personal names have been removed.
Status: review with measurements and a recommendation. The decision is yours (proposed as D-070). Measurements were taken on 2026-11-16 from the 2026-10-17 Hamilton data.

A viewer opens the Hamilton map, sees where things are, clicks a parcel, and gets its dossier (selection feedback within 100 ms, D-068). The map must work from static files, show where its background came from, and let a viewer know why a parcel cannot be selected. Parcel tiles carry the record key only (contract CN-03).

tippecanoe reported keeping "the sparsest 65.85%" of features. The z14 tile holds 3,852 parcels in both builds, so z14 and above are complete. Clicking at z12 or z13 would miss parcels without saying so.

The basemap source is not re-fetchable.

An extract from Protomaps build 20261109 returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-16; daily builds are not kept. The still render's provenance record points at a source that no longer exists, so any basemap must be archived by us (D-033) at the time it is taken.

— A. Still render only: A fixed picture of the lower city · B. Vector parcel tiles, own data: Pan, zoom and click any parcel in Hamilton, on a plain background · C. B plus self-hosted vector basemap: The same on a background with roads, water and labels · D. Third-party hosted tiles: The same as C
— A. Still render only: No · B. Vector parcel tiles, own data: Yes, from z14 · C. B plus self-hosted vector basemap: Yes, from z14 · D. Third-party hosted tiles: Yes

— A. Still render only: Yes · B. Vector parcel tiles, own data: Yes (range requests) · C. B plus self-hosted vector basemap: Yes · D. Third-party hosted tiles: Depends on someone else

— A. Still render only: Not "the actual map" · B. Vector parcel tiles, own data: No context around the parcels; low zoom · C. B plus self-hosted vector basemap: Larger payload; basemap and parcel alignment · D. Third-party hosted tiles: A dependency we do not control; conflicts with D-033 and our transparency principle

— A. Still render only: Done · B. Vector parcel tiles, own data: Small (rebuild with the contract schema) · C. B plus self-hosted vector basemap: Medium (extract, archive, style) · D. Third-party hosted tiles: Small, and we should not choose it
Do B now and C next; keep A as the first paint. Do not use D.
as the instant first paint and as the fallback when tiles fail (contract failure table). Record its dead source URL in its provenance file.

with the key as the only property, zoom 14 to 16, nothing dropped (23.4 MB; the build takes about 30 seconds). Drop
and the other properties; the shard has them.
Below z14, do not offer parcel selection.

Show the zoning and nature tiles we already have (they carry no parcel-level selection) and a plain message: "Zoom in to select a parcel". Wording goes to the label register. This is honest about why a click does nothing.
Add the basemap (C) before launch if time allows
, taken from a current Protomaps build and archived in
with its date, licence (ODbL attribution) and checksum the day it is extracted. Without it the map is parcels on a blank ground, which is workable for a first release but weak for orientation.
with their hashes. 23 MB per tile build is fine for a handful of releases in git; revisit if releases become frequent.

Transfer the archive to the data-repo work area before continuing on another machine, or fetch a fresh dated extract and record its provenance.
Package the archive and self-hosted style assets in a versioned data release, preserving ODbL attribution.
Keep the still render as first paint/fallback and wire the basemap into HeavyMap after release packaging.
Refine the low-zoom prompt and test selection latency on a mid-range phone (BL-089).
